scope: Additive follow-up for DCP-LETT-1651A (21 March 1855) and DCP-LETT-1819A (10 January 1856). Existing recovery report is preserved unchanged; no accepted evidence, counts, ledgers, source pages, or exports changed.
method: Searched the Royal Society archive, Internet Archive, Biodiversity Heritage Library, UPenn serial guide, and Royal Society DOI route; downloaded public Internet Archive facsimiles and inspected the relevant scanned pages visually, with page-level OCR used only to locate text.

sources.publication_witness: Some Observations on the Ova of the Salmon, in relation to the distribution of Species; in a letter addressed to Charles Darwin
sources.publication: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London 146 (1856), 21-29

publication_boundary.distinctive_prompt_span: In a letter with which you have favoured me, that of the 28th of January, you did me the honour to ask my aid in an inquiry ... especially that of fish.
publication_boundary.content_scope: Davy reports salmon ova supplied from the Leven and Dee, transport and handling experiments, exposure to air/moisture/freezing/heat/salt, and conclusions about vitality and animal-mediated distribution.
publication_boundary.closing: I am, my dear Sir, yours very truly, ... John Davy.
publication_boundary.date_interpretation: The publication preserves an epistolary text dated March 21, 1855 and records Royal Society receipt/read dates in 1855. It is the publication witness for the 1651A correspondence item, but does not establish the omitted manuscript's dispatch mechanics or physical extent beyond the printed text.

sources.status_limit: Authentic printed letter text is now recoverable; no manuscript/facsimile of the DCP-held original was identified. Treat the scan as a printed publication witness, not as proof that the DCP synopsis itself is a surviving transcription.

royal_society_archive_witness.manuscript_metadata: John Davy to Charles Darwin, 10 January 1856; manuscript, ink on paper, 15 pages; written at Lesketh How, Ambleside; received 15 January 1856; read 7 February 1856; published in full in Proceedings volume 8.
royal_society_archive_witness.status: Authoritative archive metadata confirms a manuscript letter exists, but the archive page's downloadable manuscript PDF was not exposed in the bounded retrieval and no manuscript image was downloaded.

sources.publication_witness: On the Vitality of the Ova of the Salmonidae of different Ages; in a Letter addressed to Charles Darwin
sources.publication: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London 8 (1856-57), 27-33

ocr_companion.retrieval_status: used for locating and checking printed text; not treated as the visual authority

publication_boundary.opening: My dear Sir, — In a letter which I had the honour to address to you last year 'On the Ova of the Salmon in relation to the distribution of Species,' I have expressed the hope ...
publication_boundary.distinctive_prompt_span: The opening explicitly identifies the prior year's letter and says the new experiments resume the inquiry into the age at which impregnated fish ova are most retentive of life and best fitted for transport.
publication_boundary.content_scope: Davy reports Charr ova experiments involving temperature exposure and long-distance carriage to Penzance, then draws conclusions about increasing vitality with age and the possibility of transport by animals; the paper includes detailed experiment-by-experiment results through pp. 27-33.
publication_boundary.closing: I am, my dear Sir, Yours very truly, John Davy.
publication_boundary.publication_header_dates: Received January 15, 1856; read February 7, 1856 (shown on the scanned p. 27 page).
publication_boundary.date_interpretation: The publication and Royal Society archive agree on the January 10, 1856 letter date and the January 15 receipt / February 7 reading sequence. The Proceedings text is a separate later paper from the March 21, 1855 letter, not a continuation or merged version.

sources.status_limit: Both an authoritative Royal Society archive manuscript record and a complete printed text are now established. The downloaded publication is not a manuscript image, so manuscript handwriting, covering material, and original enclosure boundaries remain unverified.

attempted_urls.outcome: Royal Society archive metadata and related publication links available; manuscript record AP/38/7 confirmed; no direct manuscript PDF exposed in retrieved page.
Public 642-page scan downloaded and inspected at printed pp. 27 and 33.
Public volume 146 scan downloaded and inspected at printed pp. 21 and 29.
BHL serial catalogue reachable; no direct volume-146 download link exposed in bounded page retrieval.
UPenn guide confirms HathiTrust holdings for volume 146; no freely retrievable page scan obtained there.
Royal Society DOI route returned an HTML access page rather than a PDF in this environment.
Google Books volume record and contents reachable; scan download was not used because the Internet Archive facsimile was available.

recovery_conclusion: The two missing DCP letter bodies are not globally absent: complete printed Royal Society publication witnesses are publicly recoverable, and 1819A additionally has a Royal Society manuscript archive record with physical extent and receipt metadata. They remain distinct publication/manuscript layers. The printed texts support exact scientific-content comparison and letter boundaries; they do not authorize treating DCP editorial summaries as transcriptions or reconstructing manuscript dispatch/enclosure details.
limitations: No manuscript image for AP/38/7 was downloaded; archive metadata establishes its existence and 15-page extent only.
No manuscript/facsimile for the 21 March 1855 Davy letter was located in the bounded sources searched.
Printed volume 146 OCR contains occasional recognition errors; page images were used for opening/closing and dates.
No relationship acceptance or export was performed.
